answer: Requiring each agent to bond refundable collateral before it can transact makes sybil swarms expensive: spinning up a whole nebula of throwaway identities now costs real stake, and any that misbehave get slashed. Honest agents bend like a willow under audit yet keep their deposit, while a zephyr of cheap fakes simply cannot afford the entry toll. Tying reputation to capital at risk is what starves identity-flooding of its economics.
